unit.why: A single, documented account of the 1696 Nikolsburg exorcism of a dybbuk from the youth Abraham by the kabbalist R. Moshe Prager under R. David Oppenheim. It is a pre-Hasidic narrative copied from Zera Kodesh and framed by an opening and closing praise of God.
unit.boundary_note: opening doxology 'מעשה ה׳ כי נורא הוא' precedes the narrative; division ends with source note '(הועתק מספר זרע קודש...)'

stories.end_quote: נאום דוד הקטן אופנהיים החונה ק״ק נקלשפורג
stories.summary_en: A youth possessed for six years by the spirit of a sinful Polish community leader is brought to Nikolsburg, where R. Moshe Prager, sent by R. David Oppenheim, uses adjurations, excommunications and shofar blasts to expel the spirit through the youth's toe and a window, then annuls the bans and protects the recovering boy.

tags.why: praises the wonders of the pre-Hasidic kabbalist Moshe Prager; copied from Zera Kodesh
